To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the critic of a GAN can be turned into an energy function by adding a regularization term to the generator, (2) the energy function can be used to detect anomalies and novel samples, (3) a latent space Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm can be trained to efficiently sample from this energy function, and (4) the MCMC sampler can be used to generate new samples from the energy function, and thus to generate samples from the data distribution

(1) the discriminator in GANs learns an unnormalized log-density of the training distribution, (2) adding an entropy maximization objective on the generator turns this into an energy function for the training distribution, and (3) this energy function can be used for anomaly and novelty detection.

we propose a new approach for unsupervised learning of energy-based models (EnGAN), which is able to learn an energy function and a sampling mechanism for the distribution defined by the energy function.
